searchText: I believe zkSync contracts are upgradable, so they can steal everything. As are optimism contracts IIRC. I do like that zkSync's contracts are time-locked, so even if the multi-sig (reputable people from the Ethereum ecosystem) are compromised, you still have an exit window. I believe this is an acceptable solution at this early stage, and wish Optimism, Arbitrum and others would do the same. Do you or anyone you know audit zkSync contracts on a regular basis to make sure no one is upgrading, and that no upgrades are malicious? It is strange that zksync does not even emit an event in case of the implementation upgrade, so one must periodically query `getTarget`. At least tokens like USDC have an event: https://dune.xyz/queries/97930/196681 (The implementation may emit an event, but the main proxy isn't.) No, I don't, I just use zkSync for quick payments. IIRC, there are 15 reputable people (all of whom are doxxed) on zkSync's multi-sig, and you need at least 8 of them to sign for the longest timelock. Obviously, this is a very imperfect solution, but I personally prefer it to having a completely centralized upgradability. Of course, I'd like to see immutable contracts, and they'll get there, but this is an understandable intermediate step. I agree it is better than no timelock. I just argue that it doesn't offer that much over a multisig without a timelock if there aren't easy-to-use and censorship resistant tools for monitoring the timelock by end users. Most likely attack vectors involves compromising the multi-sig accounts. A time lock does give the people with the keys some time to notice the attack. Assuming they are watching. 🙂
